correctness.rationale: For every specified pair of leaf labels, cherry contraction is a bijection to a uniform one-leaf-smaller tree with a surrogate leaf. The exact Sackin increment is \(D+2\). Counting all pairs proves the test-function identity with prefactor \(n(n-1)/(2(2n-3))\). Random orientations yield the Catalan plane-tree model; its exact weighted generating function gives the Sackin mean. An algebraic reduction gives the displayed covariance, and the exact ratio \(a_{n+1}/a_n=1+(n-2)/(n(2n-1))\) proves its zero boundaries and strictly negative sign. The central-binomial asymptotic gives the leading constant. Exact finite enumerations verify the model and all checked probability masses, but the proof of the infinite statement is analytic.

value.rationale: Cherries are a canonical local fringe-tree statistic and Sackin is a canonical global depth statistic under the PDA null model. The marked-cherry distributional transfer determines every cherry-weighted Sackin expectation; the mixed covariance is exactly zero at sizes two and three and strictly negative from size four onward, with magnitude asymptotic to a constant times \(n^{3/2}\). This establishes a structural cross-statistic relationship not recoverable from the separately published marginal means. No testing performance or other sampling-model theorem is asserted.
